summary: Multiple testimonies (between 29 and 31/12/1994) of long morning observations (by T3 and T4 of the PV) of a luminous phenomenon at low altitude in the Southeast: probable observations of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named PLERIN (22) 29.12.1994, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. This case consisted of various observations made between December 28th and 31st, 1994, in the evening or early morning in Côtes-d'Armor: four witnesses (T1, T2, T3, T4) reported their observations to the gendarmerie, and all were recorded in the same official report. The attached investigation report details all the observations and phenomena observed. The observations as a whole are rather inconsistent, with imprecise descriptions. Further examination led to the identification of three distinct phenomena: - UFO 1 observed by T1 and T2 on December 29th, 1994, between 7:00 PM and 7:30 PM. - UFOs 2, 3, and 4 seen by T3 on December 29th, 30th, and 31st between 6:00 AM and 6:45 AM (along with T4 on December 31st). - PAN 5 seen by T3 and T4 on December 31st and PAN 6 by T4 on December 28th. PAN1 presents all the characteristics of a thunderstorm observation. The lights composing the PAN are indeed compared to one or more lightning flashes: at 1, they looked like explosions but kilometers apart and always one at a time; at 2, there were lightning-like flashes in the sky; at 3, these flashes were flat and very long. I cannot tell you the size of these flashes; at 4, they looked like flashes but much bigger; at 5, a new flash appeared; at 6, when I say I saw lightning, there was only one that seemed to be moving. The hypothesis of a misinterpretation of a thunderstorm is strengthened by the fact that the UFO was seen towards the sea. This direction is also confirmed by witnesses: "I drove for a short while towards the sea," and "I saw another bright, immense blue light, in the direction of Binic, perhaps above the sea." However, the presence of a thunderstorm at sea, visible from the coast, was confirmed by the gendarmerie investigation in the early evening of December 29, 1994, that is to say, at a time consistent with the observation. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes for UFO 1: "Probable observation of a thunderstorm." UFOs 2, 3, and 4 present very similar characteristics. These are bright white lights, appearing at the same times for three consecutive days, observed for long periods (more than 40 minutes for UAPs 3 and 4), without movement, and in the same direction from one day to the next. This data is entirely characteristic of an astronomical misinterpretation. A reconstruction shows the presence of the planet Venus (very strong magnitude -4.24), in a SE direction (~130°) and about ten degrees above the horizon. The hypothesis of a Venus misinterpretation is reinforced by the fact that the UAPs were seen at a low angular altitude, through a window (the kitchen window of T3 and T4) facing SE. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes for UAPs 2, 3, and 4: B. Probable observation of Venus. The descriptions of UAPs 5 and 6 are too imprecise (short duration, little information) and too inconsistent (inconsistent testimonies) to be used: one can imagine confusion with any kind of light: car headlights, urban lights, in an emotionally charged context due to previous sightings. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes for UAPs 5 and 6: C Lack of reliable information.

summary: Multiple testimonies of successive observations (between December 28 and 31, 1994); quick observations of glows on December 31 (by T3 and his son on the report): lack of information.

summary: Multiple testimonies of observations (between 28 and 31/12/1994); Several observations on 29/12 between 19h and 1930 (by T1, T2 on PV) of white and blue lights at low altitude: probable observations of luminous phenomena coming from a storm.

summary: Multiple testimonies of successive observations (between December 28 and 31, 1994); quick observation of glows on December 28 around 7 p.m. (PAN 6 seen by T4 on the PV): lack of information.

summary: Observation of the movement of a strong green light and a bright point suddenly changing trajectory: lack of information.
description: In 2010, a person reported an observation made as a child on November 10, 1994, after 8:00 PM. A rear passenger in a vehicle traveling on a country road, he observed, heading east and through the treetops of a forest, the passage of an intense green light followed by a bright point of light located just beside it. This object suddenly changed trajectory after a significant acceleration and disappeared in a northerly direction. No unusual noise was heard during the observation. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The observation initially suggested a fireball (space debris re-entry or meteoroid), as the green color and speed were consistent with this. However, the change of direction was quite surprising: one could imagine a second fireball or shooting star starting unexpectedly at the end of the first phenomenon. Given the nature of the phenomenon and the age of the case, a subsequent investigation would not yield any new information. As GEIPAN lacks factual evidence to confirm this risky hypothesis, this case is classified as "C": Unidentifiable phenomenon: GEIPAN does not have sufficient information to provide a sound opinion.

summary: Likely sighting of a nightclub lighthouse
description: On the night of November 6-7, 1994, a young girl observed a round, luminous object with red and white lights in the sky. This phenomenon was accompanied by muffled, repetitive noises. Her grandmother also witnessed the phenomenon. The description suggests it was likely a nightclub advertising beacon, the muffled noise probably being the propagation of low frequencies from the sound system.

summary: Observation of a nightclub advertising projector
description: On November 4, 1994, at approximately 9:45 PM, seven witnesses observed a series of white lights swirling in the sky for about fifteen minutes. These lights were quickly identified as an advertising spotlight installed on a nearby nightclub.

summary: sighting of a UFO that appeared to be following the witnesses
description: On October 30, 1994, at approximately 1:45 AM, a couple in a car observed a luminous circle rotating on its axis, with regularly spaced lights around its periphery. The phenomenon was estimated to be 5 to 6 meters high and stationary above the car. The car quickly left the city but encountered the phenomenon again a short distance away: a triangle with the same type of light around its perimeter had appeared alongside the circle. The triangle was equilateral, approximately 10 meters on each side, and at an altitude of 10 to 15 meters. The phenomenon accompanied the vehicle, which was traveling at approximately 80 km/h, adapting to its speed, for several kilometers. During a change of direction, the object accelerated and moved away; the witnesses then described it as having the shape of a boomerang. During the same time slot and on the same road, another couple in a different car described the phenomenon with surprisingly similar terminology and observed the same changes in their vehicle. This phenomenon could not be explained.

summary: Observations of a stationary luminous phenomenon in the sky followed by its rapid disappearance.
description: On the afternoon of October 28, 1994, in the Gard and Hérault departments, witnesses observed a stationary luminous phenomenon. Some witnesses, equipped with a zoom camera, saw the object with a distinctive shape formed by points of light. A less intense light could be distinguished in the center. The witnesses then witnessed the object split in two. The observation ended with the luminous phenomenon disappearing at very high speed. No photographs were taken. No other information could be gathered.

summary: Observation from an aircraft and on the ground of a probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On October 28, 1994, at 6:57 PM, the pilot of a Dornier 228 aircraft, while hovering at 10,000 feet, reported unidentified traffic. He described it as an intense light with a significant yellow-orange trail moving at very high speed as it passed over the aircraft in a west-east direction. The co-pilot confirmed the phenomenon, although their estimates of its duration differed (12 seconds to 1 minute). Two other witnesses on the ground also reported seeing a bright light for about ten seconds. The air traffic was well-known and could not explain the phenomenon. The most likely hypothesis is that of atmospheric reentry.

summary: A rapid passage of three luminous orbs
description: On October 20, 1994, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness observed three luminous, yellowish orbs passing briefly above his home, aligned in a line. No sound was heard. No other information is available.

summary: Discovery of circles of pebbles on the ground
description: On October 18, 1994, around 2 p.m., a gendarme on leave, while picking mushrooms, discovered a circle on the ground made of shards of stone resembling clinker. The leaves that came into contact with the stones had turned a sulfurous green. As night fell, he decided to return the next day but could not find the spot.

summary: Long observations of the silent low-altitude evolutions of a luminous object: probable observations of a Mylar balloon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named LAVOUTE-CHILHAC (43) 09.10.1994, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On October 9, 1994, at approximately 9:45 a.m., a witness (T1) present during a hunt observed the silent movements of a white, cylindrical, luminous object with silvery metallic reflections for 25 to 30 minutes. The witness also observed blue and red lights. He followed it with his eyes until it was out of sight. Later, upon meeting his brother (T2), the latter recounted that, near his home around 9:30 a.m., he too had seen a luminous object that intrigued him. T2 described an object that was cylindrical at the top and semicircular at the bottom, reflecting the sun and moving across the landscape. After 30 minutes of observation, this witness decided to stop following the object. The physical characteristics (shape, but especially metallic appearance and mention by the witnesses of silvery reflections) and dynamic characteristics (slow, primarily horizontal movements, close to the ground and in a depression, generated by the local weather conditions in the mountainous area that morning) are entirely consistent with the hypothesis of confusion with a metallized nylon balloon of the Mylar type. One of the witnesses (T2) also suggested a balloon (see the investigation report). At the start of the observation, the sun had not yet had time to heat the parts of the atmosphere closest to the ground, particularly those sheltered in depressions. Thus, the Mylar balloon was still subject to local conditions of weak or nonexistent sunlight and very weak local currents, causing it to drift with these currents, remaining close to the ground. This state persisted until, as the sun rose higher, it managed to warm the balloon's envelope, causing the air inside to expand. This resulted in the balloon becoming lighter than the surrounding air and thus leaving the ground to rise slowly and steadily to altitude, as described by witness T1 at the end of the observation. It is entirely plausible that this balloon was already present the previous evening. It was a Saturday. The balloon was likely launched from a neighboring village. The temperature dropping at nightfall caused the air inside to contract, making it sink to the ground in a depression, from which it only emerged the following morning when temperatures became favorable again. The case is well-supported, with two very precise, independent witness statements and an investigation by the local police, who drew up a site plan. At the time of the observation, GEIPAN had little to no experience with balloon cases. This has changed since then (search the website www.geipan using the keywords "balloon" or "Mylar"). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a Mylar balloon.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On September 25, 1994, at approximately 6:10 a.m., a witness observed from his bedroom the rapid descent of a blue ball behind a nearby quarry. No sound was heard, but blue lights rose behind the mountain after the presumed fall. The witness woke his partner, who only observed the lights behind the quarry. It was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a bright light followed by a geometric shape. Lack of information.
description: On October 16, 1994, at approximately 10:30 PM, a witness observed a bright yellow light at a distance of about 200 meters. Then, a reddish-orange geometric shape (hexagonal or octagonal) rose above the woods from which the light originated. No noise was heard during this observation. No other witness statements were collected. No unusual traces were observed in the area indicated by the witness. No further information could be gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Fleeting observation of an ovoede luminous phenomenon
description: On September 11, 1994, at approximately 11:30 PM, three witnesses in a car observed a fleeting, luminous, ovoid shape. These individuals were specifically "searching for UFOs." One of the witnesses, however, remained skeptical, believing it to be a simple illumination from a vehicle's headlights. The theft of equipment from a nearby construction site that same night seemed to support this theory, but no further information was available.

summary: Observation of a cylindrical-shaped device.
description: Recent testimony (October 13, 2009) of an earlier sighting (August 28, 1994). During a picnic, four members of the same family observed a particular object approaching. A huge, copper-colored cylinder with portholes appeared. It remained stationary 10 to 15 meters above the ground, then changed direction and speed before disappearing instantly. No photographs of the craft or the site were taken at the time. The age of the case makes any investigation difficult, if not impossible.

summary: Observation of fleeting luminous phenomena
description: A fleeting observation of luminous phenomena in the sky. The two witnesses describe different phenomena, and the dates do not match either.

summary: Observation of a horseshoe-shaped luminous phenomenon
description: On August 17, 1994, at approximately 12:30 a.m., a witness observed a luminous horseshoe-shaped object in the sky with undefined edges and yellow, orange, and green lights. The observation was very brief, lasting about four seconds. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of a disco laser projector
description: During the night of August 12-13, 1994, between 1:00 and 1:30 AM, four witnesses reported seeing a white ball spinning in the sky along a road for approximately 14 km. The investigation quickly revealed that it was the sighting of a "skyrose" type laser projector being used on a trial basis by a nightclub located about 6 km from the observation site.

summary: Observation of the passage of a dark, triangular shape.
description: Recent testimony (August 23, 2008) of an earlier observation: On August 12, 1994, at 11:45 PM, a group of people were walking away from a seaside village. The person at the front suddenly had their attention drawn to a stationary black mass above them. For six seconds, they observed an enormous triangular shape bordered on two sides by small lights of varying intensity and alignment. Two children also observed this triangle, which, in total silence, then rotated on its axis and moved off to the southeast, disappearing over the horizon. The witness noted all of this in a sketchbook and attached an illustration of their observation to their testimony. No other testimonies have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which any investigation is currently impossible.

summary: Fleeting observation of a small luminous sphere
description: During the night of August 9-10, 1994, at approximately 12:30 a.m., a witness observed a small, luminous sphere moving very quickly across the sky for a few seconds. No sound or trail accompanied this phenomenon. No other information has been collected about it.

summary: observation of small craters containing pieces of stone.
description: On the morning of July 31, 1994, a witness noticed small craters in his garden, clustered in four areas. The grass was withered all around these craters, which contained pieces of stone. It was probably a meteorite impact.

summary: Observations of a luminous phenomenon in the shape of a hemisphere and in colours varying from red to yellow: mistaken for a moonrise.
description: Two witnesses reported seeing, on July 31, 1994, around 1:15 a.m., just above the hills east of Marseille, a red hemisphere twice the size of the moon, turning yellow as it shrank. The witnesses observed the phenomenon disappearing in a thin ray of light. They could not explain what they saw. This case was initially classified as "C" due to a lack of information. In July 2012, a reconstruction at the same location and time was conducted as part of a possible Saros cycle (see explanations in the investigation report). After a completely conclusive reconstruction 18 years later, GEIPAN classified this case as "A": mistaken for the moon at its rising.

summary: Daytime observation of the silent movement of a cylindrical object associated with two round, metallic-colored shapes moving in all directions: probable observation of a balloon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification, explicitly stated in the investigation report. This observation, previously named PLAN DE CUQUES (13) 1994, is one of the cases classified as "D" at the time and has recently been re-examined. On July 31, 1994, around 2:30 PM, witnesses observed a cylindrical shape in the sky associated with two round, metallic-colored shapes. One of the witnesses saw two protrusions with flashing lights. This object moved silently, flying in all directions at a fairly high altitude. Two witnesses reported their observations to the police. Several elements suggest it was mistaken for a novelty balloon, tossed about by the wind at altitude (see the investigation report): - the direction of movement, consistent with the wind direction. Witness #1 provided fairly precise geographical information allowing the UFO's trajectory to be reconstructed, indicating that it was moving along a generally south-north axis, entirely consistent with the wind direction recorded by the Marseille-Observatory station. - the way the UFO moved. This was described by the witnesses as follows: It flew rather slowly and circled. It had the attitude of a falling leaf, while maintaining its direction... it flew rapidly in all directions... to the object that kept swaying. This description is typical of light objects carried and tossed by a light wind. - the description of the UFO. Witnesses describe a cylindrical shape, about the size of two vehicles, metallic in color, with two sort of ears on the side. I also noticed two round things, like car headlights... a more or less round shape of metallic color... above this object [were] two protrusions with flashing lights. The mention of flashing lights is related to the mention of a metallic-colored object. If the object is partially made of a highly reflective material, such as Mylar, and other non-reflective materials, its movement in the wind, causing it to spin in all directions, and the sun's rays reflecting randomly off its surface, will give witnesses the impression of flashing lights. It could therefore be a novelty beach ball, released from Cassis and its surroundings, which are located along the extension of the UFO's trajectory, to the south, and where many places are suitable for summer leisure activities (beaches, coves, etc.), particularly in broad daylight, on a summer Saturday. No other eyewitness accounts have been collected, even though the sighting occurred in broad daylight, on a summer Saturday, in an inhabited area (the village of Allauch). This also supports a low-strange hypothesis, such as the one, argued elsewhere, of a novelty balloon. The consistency of the testimonies is rather weak. Although we have two testimonies, they are very brief and come from dependent witnesses (friends). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: a balloon.

summary: Probable sighting of a weather balloon
description: On July 29, 1994, around 3 a.m., an insomniac witness observed a luminous, round shape with flashes of light around its perimeter from his bedroom. The most likely hypothesis, put forward after a brief investigation, was the observation of a weather balloon.

summary: Observations of the movement of luminous spheres.
description: A witness reports that as a child, during the summer of 1994 (the witness no longer remembers the exact month and day; these are given here arbitrarily), he observed the movement of a luminous sphere. This sphere, reddish-orange in color, was the size of a marble and was very close to the witness. It moved silently. The witness was, and remains, deeply impressed. On two occasions in 2006, this same witness observed the furtive and more distant movement of luminous spheres. No other reports of similar sightings in the area have been collected by the gendarmerie. Despite an IPN (National Police Information) investigation with the witness, this recent testimony of earlier sightings lacks sufficient data.

summary: Observation of 3 triangular or pyramidal objects flying over the witness's car at low altitude
description: On June 27, 1994, at approximately 11:00 AM, a witness driving a car observed two dark, pyramidal shapes, without lights or illumination, at an estimated distance of 8 km. The witness lost sight of these two objects as he turned a bend in the road. A short distance further on, he spotted a third, black, triangular shape flying above his car at the same speed, approximately 80 km/h. Within moments, the object accelerated and disappeared with a muffled sound and a high-pitched hiss. The phenomenon observed by the witness remains unexplained.

summary: Observation of a stationary triangular shape
description: On June 24, 1994, at approximately 2:40 a.m., during a night patrol, three gendarmes noticed lights above the highway. Upon approaching, they determined that the lights were emanating from a stationary triangular object at an unspecified distance from the ground. After stopping their vehicle, the object slowly approached and hovered above the gendarmes' car. When they restarted the engine, the object sped off, disappearing into thin air. While unable to pinpoint the exact moment, the gendarmes also noticed their communication equipment in the vehicle stop working. The observation lasted approximately 10 minutes; no noise or smoke was observed. No explanation could be found for this phenomenon.

summary: Observing lights in the night.
description: Recent testimony (June 3, 2009) of an earlier observation (June 23, 1994, around 11:00-11:30 PM). A witness recounts seeing, from a skylight, a group of six lights above the forest for 5 to 10 minutes. These lights were initially stationary, then began to rotate on an axis before disappearing. No noise was heard during the observation. The witness reports that an EDF transformer on the power line crossing this part of the forest was quickly replaced after that night. No other testimonies concerning this phenomenon have been collected, and we lack information about it.

summary: Observation of a luminous sphere
description: On June 22, 194, a witness reported seeing a luminous sphere from their vehicle descend to the ground, then take off again, splitting into three. The following day, local gendarmes found soldiers using a cannon in an ambush at the observation site. Although we have no further information, these military maneuvers taking place in the area could explain the observed phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a lemon-shaped object accompanying the witness's vehicle
description: On June 11, 1994, at approximately 11:45 PM, a witness driving his car observed a lemon-shaped object on the side of the road. It had a cable attached to its top and was dotted with numerous lights. Having slowed to around 20 km/h, the object continued moving at roughly the same speed. As the car caught up with it, the object split in two, maintaining its shape and size. The object then accelerated, turned to the right, passed over a clump of trees, and then rapidly moved vertically. This observation of a silent phenomenon, lasting several minutes, remains unexplained.

summary: Likely sighting of a child's balloon
description: On May 14, 1994, at approximately 9:20 PM, four witnesses observed, photographed, and filmed the movement of an oval object in the sky. In a nearby field and in the neighboring canton, fragments of balloons were discovered, along with cards from a balloon-launching contest. This children's contest had originated in England. The observed phenomenon was therefore likely one of these balloons.

summary: Observation of a Y-shaped light phenomenon
description: On May 9, 1994, at approximately 4:30 a.m., a witness who was awake observed a powerful Y-shaped luminous phenomenon for several minutes. After a few minutes during which the phenomenon remained stationary, it moved away and gradually disappeared. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Likely sighting of a space vehicle
description: On May 7, 1994, at approximately 9:30 PM, three witnesses observed a particularly bright point of light moving very slowly across the sky. This observation, which lasted several tens of minutes, was likely that of a spacecraft, as one of the witnesses made the same observation the following day.

summary: Likely observation of a celestial body
description: On April 14, 1994, around 10 p.m. and later that night, a witness observed a fixed and flashing point of light. During the observation, this point moved slightly, like the stars. It was likely the observation of a celestial body.

summary: Long observation of a white glow in the night sky and sudden disappearance: lack of information.
description: Recent report (December 6, 2014) of an old observation without a specific date. In April 1994, around 10 PM, a witness and his friend first observed a lenticular-shaped white glow in the sky. One of the witnesses thought it was an object, present for over an hour and a half, and estimated its height at 300 meters. The object appeared to move back and forth and then suddenly disappeared, as if drawn upwards. This long observation (1 hour 30 minutes) of a white glow low on the horizon simply suggested the Moon, perhaps partially obscured by clouds, and then disappearing behind a cloud. This type of misinterpretation is common. The lack of a precise date makes it impossible to verify or refute this hypothesis. This case is classified as "C" due to the lack of precise information about the date of the event.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On March 18, 1994, several witnesses observed a bright yellow ball, resembling a shooting star, passing rapidly by. The witnesses' descriptions suggest that it was an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of an isosceles triangle shape.
description: On March 18, 1994, a witness observed an isosceles triangle shape for a few moments. No other information is available.

summary: Likely observation of a laser beam
description: On March 17, 1994, around 8:00 PM, a witness alerted the police that he had observed a turquoise-green light with a red dot rotating at high speed above the sea. The police patrolled for about an hour but did not observe the phenomenon. That same evening, students from a local school were observing the sky to watch Jupiter rise but saw nothing further. On April 3, the phenomenon recurred, and the observation was reported by several witnesses. No aircraft was identified, but the characteristics of the observation suggested reflections from the use of a laser.

summary: Observation in a passing cloud of a large, bright orange crescent: astronomical observation of the Moon.
description: This observation case is classified as C by SEPRA, under the name EPINAC (71) 16.03.1994: it is currently under review (see the Investigation Notes document). On March 16, 1994, at 8:10 or 8:30 PM, in Tintry (71), a person walking home observed a milky cloud in front of them, which, on three occasions, for a few seconds each, revealed a large, luminous orange crescent. No other witness statements were collected during the police investigation. This case is not very substantial (only one witness), but the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the crescent Moon, seen through a cloud layer. Furthermore, the Moon was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky. The issue is not the witness's visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their own experience (fatigue, partial observation of the Moon through a cloud). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a weak anomaly is classified as "A," an observation linked to a misidentification of the Moon.

summary: Observation of the movement of an object in the sky. An old observation.
description: On March 5, 2009, a witness reported to GEIPAN an observation lasting only a few seconds that occurred on March 13, 1994. Between 5:00 PM and 5:20 PM, on a road leading to Ploubalay, the witness saw an object moving very rapidly northward on a slightly inclined trajectory. The object disappeared into the clouds. No precise information could be gathered regarding the shape and dimensions of the object seen at high altitude. The age of the observation and the lack of information make any investigation difficult, if not impossible.

summary: Short observations of the movement of colored lights outlining a shape in the sky: probable observations of a helicopter.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named MESSINCOURT (08) 10.03.1994, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On March 10, 1994, at approximately 8:55 PM, two witnesses observed colored lights outlining a shape (circular and flat for T1 and triangular for T2) in the sky. The unusual trajectory intrigued the witnesses, as did the arrival of another UFO. No unusual noises were heard during the brief, intermittent observation by the two witnesses. No other testimonies were collected. Only one hypothesis could be considered: that of a helicopter. Two very strong elements in the testimonies strongly support this hypothesis and are consistent between witnesses: the trajectory and, above all, the triangle of three navigation lights (white, red, and green). The absence of radar detection could be explained by a low altitude (< 200 or 300 m), which is unconfirmed but consistent with the other observed elements. Similarly, the absence of noise perception (perceived by T2, T1 did not comment) may seem surprising but has been encountered by GEIPAN in a few similar cases. It is also known that attention focused on a very striking visual observation can mask the accompanying auditory perception. The other opposing elements cannot invalidate the hypothesis because their reliability is questionable due to a lack of confirmation or even disagreement between witnesses. Even assuming they are reliable, explanations can be found that do not reduce the probability of the hypothesis by 50%. This is the second UFO, similar to the first, since at T1, white lights were seen orbiting (according to T2) or slowly rotating (according to T1), either inside the navigation triangle (according to T1) or outside it (according to T2). The testimonies would have justified an on-site investigation to clarify the information and understand the discrepancies. Nevertheless, the consistency is sufficient to draw a conclusion because the observation is quite long and detailed, and concordant on the key points (both positive and negative). Details seen by T1 are not seen by T2 (which is not a contradiction), and the true contradictions (shape and positions of the white lights) are ultimately not decisive. Consequently, GEIPAN considers the helicopter hypothesis to have a probability greater than 50%: classification B: helicopter.

summary: Observation of luminous points in a triangular shape.
description: On March 5, 1994, four witnesses went to the Col de Vence to try and spot unidentified aerial phenomena. They did indeed observe three luminous points forming a triangle that appeared to be approaching them. The phenomenon remained silent and was observed for approximately one and a half minutes. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Likely observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On February 5, 1994, at approximately 8:00 AM, a woman driving her car observed a luminous sphere passing by very quickly for a few seconds. This sphere was also seen by another motorist who reported it over CB radio. It was likely an atmospheric reentry event.

summary: Aircraft crossing paths with a phenomenon confirmed by radar. Instantaneous disappearance.
description: On January 28, 1994, at 1:14 PM, the crew of an Air France Airbus A320-11 flying from Nice to London observed an unexplained phenomenon. While flying over the Coulommiers region in Seine-et-Marne, the chief flight attendant, who was in the cockpit at the time, reported a phenomenon to the captain on the left side of the aircraft that he thought might be a weather balloon. The captain and first officer described seeing a dark brown or red disc that changed shape before suddenly disappearing. The captain reported the incident to air traffic control in Reims, who confirmed that there was no air traffic in the area. At the same time, an unidentified radar track was detected by the radar at Cinq-Mars-la-Pile. This radar signature, recorded for 50 seconds, does indeed cross the trajectory of flight AF3532 but does not correspond to any filed flight plan and disappears simultaneously from the crew's view and radar screens. Three years later, when the case is reported in the press, witnesses provide their testimony by filing an official report with the gendarmerie and SEPRA (the Aerospace Rare Phenomena Expertise Service at CNES). Investigators remain cautious regarding the correlation between the radar signature and the phenomenon. Even if the radar signature does not correspond to the observation, the phenomenon is not an aircraft, since there would then have been a corresponding radar signature. In 2012, a new verification was requested from Météo-France to study the hypothesis of a weather balloon sighting (see attached). A weather balloon did indeed cross the aircraft's trajectory, but one hour before the sighting. At the time of the observation, the balloon burst and was expected to drift far to the southeast of the aircraft. This case therefore remains unexplained, with coherent eyewitness accounts for a truly strange sighting. Two hypotheses can still be considered, but are impossible to substantiate: a previously unknown atmospheric optics phenomenon or a flexible object (e.g., a balloon envelope) drifting with the wind. This case is classified as D1: a moderately consistent unexplained case with a marked degree of strangeness. The late witness statements, the absence of the flight attendant's testimony, and the radar trace's inconsistency with the observed object weaken the case's credibility.

summary: Likely observation of a laser projector
description: On January 10, 1994, around 5 a.m., a couple observed a luminous oval shape from their home. It moved back and forth in the air without ever touching the ground. A whistling sound was also heard. The investigation revealed that it was likely a laser advertising projector being tested at a nearby nightclub. The phenomenon was also observed in several neighboring towns, where witnesses had been notified of the projector's testing.

summary: Successive nighttime observations of a silent phenomenon of varied shape (rectangular, rhombus and ovoid) with colored lights (white, red, orange): lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named CHARLEVILLE-MEZIERES (08) 09.01.1994, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On January 9, 1994, at approximately 7:45 PM, the front-seat passenger (T1) of a vehicle observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky that intrigued her. On several occasions and in different locations, the witness observed a rectangular shape, then a diamond shape, and finally an oval shape with lights of different colors. No unusual noises were heard. The witness suddenly became frightened as the shape appeared to be moving towards her. The witness went to the police station, and the driver (T2), who had not been able to make all the same observations as his passenger, verbally confirmed her account. No other witness statements or information were gathered during the police investigation. Despite the police investigation, many basic elements necessary for any analysis of this type are missing (see the investigation report). For each phase: - the azimuth or a directional reference point at which the UFO was located; - the elevation above the horizon; - the duration of the observation; - the angular dimensions of the UFO. We have a second witness, T2, who claims to confirm T1's statements, but at the same time indicates that he only saw the UFO at point ne3 and never afterward, without making or signing any statement. Therefore, we don't know if the UFO sighting at point 3 coincides with T1's. The fact that T1 didn't share his second observation at point ne5 with T2, and that T2 didn't testify, also undermines the overall consistency, which is already significantly hampered by a lack of precision. The consistency (level and reliability of the information) of the testimony is too weak to construct a hypothesis or draw any conclusions. In this context, the strange and inexplicable nature that may have prevailed during the initial investigation cannot be considered valid. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.
